newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold again with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold again with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly stayed unchanged on Wednesday in thin trade, helped by a slightly firmer crude market and prospects for better utility buying once hotter weather kicks in, market sources said.

"The market feels stable to firm, but there's not a lot of demand. We're just waiting for the heat," said one cash trader, noting fairly mild eastern and southern weather was hampering utility demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was still quoted in the $16.50-$16.75 a barrel area, while 0.3 percent high pour notionally edged up slightly to the low-$17s, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York held relatively steady, with three percent still talked on either side of $14.50.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent remained quoted at $16.25, while three percent also was little changed at $14.25-$14.50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate June gas prices slipped about 10 cents to about the $2.50/mmBtu area, or $15.75 a barrel equivalent. June gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell by about a nickel to $2.29/mmBtu, or $14.43 a barrel.
